text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
ALL NEWSPAPERS
- A row over a law on customs tariffs continued through the night as the right-wing opposition took every opportunity to delay the debate.
- An international conference was held to mark the 5th anniversary of Estonia's national currency.
- State examinations showed a generally low standard of knowledge among school-leavers
SONUMILEHT
- The Reform Party declared yesterday that it is firmly in the opposition, although it won't provoke early elections.
- The government decided to exempts investments from income tax in all regions except Tallinn.
- MPs Andres Tarand and Toivo Jurgenson claimed at a news conference that officials have sufficient information to plan the future of the state but they fail to use it properly.
EESTI PAEVALEHT
- Prime Minister Mart Siimann will have to explain to parliament the government's decision to reject the Chechen delegation's visa application.
- Estonian EU ambassador Clyde Kull described the Amsterdam EU summit as not threatening Estonia's interests.
POSTIMEES
- the Estonian Olympic Committee announced bonuses for medal winners at the next games: one million kroons to gold medal winners, 700,000 kroons for silver and 500,000 kroons for bronze.
- Only 35 students from an initial 300 volunteers arrived for tests to begin training as reserve officers.
- The government decided to form a commission for solving problems with non-citizens.
ARIPAEV
- The AGA company has exhausted its carbon dioxide reserves after the Moe distillery closed down. Unless the production can be restarted, gas will have to be bought from Russia at a higher price.
- The police have initiated an investigation of share deals in Rakvere.
- The government will not participate in the Plaza conference hotel project in Tallinn.
-- Riga newsroom, +371 721 5240
